arcReviewReport.finalArc:
1. Every autumn Saturday, Mama waits over by the Wasserkirche while Levin, Julian, Max and Kiaan visit the old dragon Funkenherz, who sleeps in the quiet corner beside the Grossmünster and flies off from any grown-up who comes near.
2. She lets them warm their cold hands at the golden scale over her heart, because her fire lives in it, and it must never go cold, she says.
3. But this Saturday that scale, as big as Levin's hand, lies on the autumn pavement, still warm, and Funkenherz beside the church wall is grey instead of red.
4. Levin wants to warn her that her fire has fallen out, but his voice comes out so small that Funkenherz, pretending all is well, flies off to the wooded hill by the zoo, where she goes when she wants to be alone among animals.
5. Because the scale is getting cooler in his hand, Levin asks Mama to take them to the zoo, and Mama rides the tram up the hill with all four.
6. On the tram the scale grows cooler still, so Julian, who remembers how Funkenherz warmed his cold hands, tucks it under his jacket against his warm tummy and will not give it back or let Levin go looking without him.
7. At the zoo, Mama waits on the bench by the flamingo pond, as she always waits by the Wasserkirche, and warns: "Stay away from the water, and stay together!"
8. So Kiaan, looking hard at the ground, spots huge claw prints in the wet leaves along the pond's edge.
9. But as they follow the prints, Julian slips, the scale slides out of his jacket toward the cold water, and Max leaps and catches it just in time, though it is colder now.
10. The prints lead away from the path into the fog between the trees, where a big grey rock opens one golden eye, and for the first time the children see that no warm steam rises from Funkenherz's back.
11. "I am only resting, go back to your Mama," she says with her face turned away, and because all four talk at once and Levin's voice stays small, she never hears about the scale.
12. Instead she flies slowly over the high zoo fence into the foggy wood, where no child can climb after her.
13. Now Funkenherz is gone in the fog, and under Julian's jacket only one tiny warm spot is left on the scale.
14. Twice Levin's small voice came too late, so he stretches out both arms and calls with his whole voice: "Funkenherz! Your heart-scale is here! Your fire is not gone!"
15. The big voice carries through the fog, and Funkenherz, who thought her fire was simply burning out with age, turns, glides back over the fence and lowers her chest to the children.
16. Julian's knees shake in front of the huge dragon, but he steps forward and presses the scale into the empty place over her heart.
17. The last spark jumps into her, her scales glow red again, and warm steam rises from her back.
18. Funkenherz curls her warm tail around all four, breathes warm air over their cold hands and says, "Thank you, Levin, for your big voice, and thank you, Julian, for keeping my fire warm," and Levin feels brave.

Challenges taken:
1. Funkenherz does not know her fire has fallen out.
2. She refuses the help the children bring.
3. Finding the hidden dragon among the zoo's trees and animals.
4. Small, slow Julian is not left behind.
5. Levin calls out loud although his voice is shy.
arcReviewReport.arcHints:
ISSUE (s5): The scale is on the pavement in s3 yet already cooling in Levin's hand in s5 with no pickup shown. → CHANGE: Open s5 with Levin lifting the still-warm scale from the stones before he asks Mama for the tram.
ISSUE (s9): Max catches the sliding scale but nothing gives it back, yet s13 has it under Julian's jacket again. → CHANGE: After the catch, Max pushes the colder scale straight back under Julian's jacket.
ISSUE (s18): Funkenherz thanks only Levin and Julian, so Max's catch and Kiaan's tracking go unacknowledged. → CHANGE: She also thanks Max for the catch and Kiaan for the prints as her tail curls around all four.
arcReviewReport.logic:
Want and stakes: Levin wants to get Funkenherz's fallen heart-scale back onto her while it is still warm; if it goes cold first, her fire is gone forever and she can never fly or warm anyone again. The deadline is the scale itself, which cools a little more with every hour.
Opposition: Funkenherz herself — sure her fire is simply burning out with age and ashamed to be seen grey and cold, she flies off, hides and turns the children away.
Facts:
- Levin (commissioned) — knows the golden scale over Funkenherz's heart is where her fire lives; his voice goes small just when it matters.
- Julian (commissioned) — stubborn, he holds on to what he carries and will not stay behind; he is small and clumsy on wet leaves.
- Max (commissioned) — fast enough to catch a falling thing; he talks loudly and all at once.
- Kiaan (commissioned) — attentive, he notices small marks on the ground.
- Funkenherz (commissioned) — can still fly while any spark is left in her; she has not seen that her heart-scale fell off while she slept.
- Mama (new) — takes the children by tram and waits apart, since Funkenherz flies from grown-ups.
- Rule of the world: Funkenherz's fire lives in the golden scale over her heart, as big as Levin's hand. Pressed back while warm, it relights her fire; once cold, her fire is gone forever. A warm dragon's back steams in the cold; a cold one does not.
- Rule of the world: any grown-up who comes near makes Funkenherz fly away, so she sleeps in the quiet corner beside the Grossmünster where only children come to her, and in the zoo she stays deep in the foggy trees, far from the paths where grown-ups walk.
Motives:
- Levin: loves the dragon friend who warms his hands every Saturday → follows her and in the end calls her with his whole voice.
- Julian: will not let his big brother go without him and wants to help; he remembers Funkenherz warming their cold hands on her scale and thinks his warm tummy can do the same for the scale → tucks it under his jacket, comes along and presses it back.
- Max: quick and brave, he loves an adventure → leaps and catches the sliding scale.
- Kiaan: wants to find Funkenherz and looks carefully → spots her claw prints.
- Funkenherz: ashamed to be seen cold and believing her fire is ending anyway → flies to the wooded hill by the zoo, where she goes when she wants to be alone among animals, hides there and sends the children away. When she hears her fire is found, she wants it back more than anything → she returns.
- Mama: trusts the children and knows Funkenherz flees grown-ups → takes them to the zoo, waits on a bench by the flamingo pond and warns them about the water.
Central figure: Funkenherz
Events: 5
Chain:
- Because the warm golden scale lies on the autumn pavement beside the Grossmünster, and grey Funkenherz flies off to her quiet hill before shy Levin's small voice reaches her, Levin sets out to bring her fire back. It costs him the one chance to tell her right there.
- Because the scale cools on the way, Julian, who remembers her warming his hands, tucks it against his warm tummy and refuses to stay behind. The scale cools more slowly now, but the smallest child carries it.
- But at the zoo, as they follow Kiaan's claw prints along the pond, Julian slips and the scale slides toward the cold water. Max catches it just in time, but it is colder now.
- But when the prints lead into the trees to Funkenherz in the fog, with no warmth rising from her back, she turns her face away and sends them off. Because all four talk at once and Levin's voice stays small, she never hears about the scale and flies over the high zoo fence. This is the low point: she is gone, the fence cannot be climbed, and one warm spot is left on the scale.
- Because Levin's small voice has come too late twice, he now calls with his whole voice the one thing she never heard, that her scale is here. It carries over the fence where no child can follow, and she comes back because she wants her fire. The scale still relights her fire when Julian presses it on, because he kept its last spark warm.
